name: Conservative democracy
summary: Conservative democracy (muhafazakâr demokrasi) is the political identity Turkey's Justice and Development Party (AKP) adopted after 2002 to mark its break with the Islamist National Outlook tradition. It presents conservatism as gradual change that keeps 'perennial' values (family, religion as a social value, national culture) inside a democratic, pluralist and rule-of-law framework: legitimacy rests on the will of the people, secularism means the state's impartiality towards all beliefs rather than hostility to religion, politics is a realm of compromise, and the economy is a market economy with a social state. Its programme sought EU membership, civilian control of the military and wider cultural rights.
scope: As the defining scholarship sets it out: Çağlıyan-İçener (Turkish Studies 2009) treats conservative democracy as the AKP's self-defining concept, formulated by its leaders and theorist Yalçın Akdoğan and resting on the party programme; Kaddorah (ACRPS 2015) and Aslan (AJISS 2013) analyse it from the party's programme, Akdoğan's writings and the 2012 'Political Vision of AK Parti 2023', which opens with a section on the 'conservative democrat political identity'. The profile is answered from that scholarship, the AKP programme (2001) and the 2012 Political Vision. As the doctrine of a party that governed alone, its record counts too: the acts of AKP governments up to 2012 as the Vision and Çağlıyan-İçener report them answer statements on their own (record over words). Erdoğan's later rule (post-2013, the 2017 presidential system), which the scholarship treats under other labels such as Erdoğanism and which these defining sources do not document, is not covered; nor are critics' readings of a 'hidden agenda'. Conservatism and democracy in general, and the US 'Conservative Democrats', are other subjects.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The Vision wants Turkey's military defence 'more efficient, deterrent and modern' and its own tanks and drones.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The programme plans closer coordination between the Treasury and the Central Bank and fights inflation through monetary stability, assuming a central bank.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The programme says that in democracies 'it is not possible for some of the citizens to benefit from higher rights and freedoms or privileges'.

abolish-ip.rationale: The programme promises to 'protect patent and license rights with an understanding suitable to international standards'.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Vision promises social policy that 'strengthen[s] the institution of marriage', and the programme offers marriage loans.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The programme is built on a market economy, wage policy (a revised minimum wage, equal pay) and 'an earnings system based on production'.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The programme modernizes penal institutions and makes justice and security basic state functions.

abolish-wage-labour.rationale: The programme's labour policy rests on employment, minimum wages and equal pay within a market economy.

all-land-state-owned.rationale: The programme guarantees property rights and supports private forestry, though forest land stays state property.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The programme's secularism lets people without beliefs organize their lives freely, and Erdoğan, quoted by Kaddorah, says the secular state 'has even to respect and defend atheists'.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: On the Arab uprisings the Vision insists that change 'must take place peacefully and with national consensus'.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The programme wants youth centres abroad so that Turkish emigrants are not 'estranged from their own cultures and becoming assimilated'.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments cut the budget deficit 'by maintaining fiscal discipline' and public net debt from 74% to 39.4% of GDP, and promises fiscal discipline will be strictly followed.

ban-cartels.rationale: The programme promises to eliminate unfair competition and 'not allowing monopolization', including in the media.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments made party closures more difficult and pledges laws so that crimes are punished in members, not by closing parties.

ban-interest.rationale: The Vision aims to keep interest rates in single digits within a liberal financial system, though the programme prefers earnings from production 'rather than collecting interest'.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Under 'Budget Rights' the programme wants parliament more effective in preparing and auditing the government's budget.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: The Vision calls political parties 'indispensable actors in a democracy' and gives NGOs and professional bodies a key role.

capital-controls.rationale: The Vision says 'we will continue to support free capital movements and free trade' with floating exchange rates.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The programme promises precautions against broadcasts on alcohol, drugs, violence and pornography that harm youth, but prefers media self-control and free expression.

central-planning.rationale: The programme 'favors market economy operating with all its institutions and rules' and holds that the state should stay out of economic activity in principle.

change-traditions-that-no-longer-suit.rationale: The Vision wants to 're-formulate our values ... to respond the needs of our time' while conserving perennial values and core traditions.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments built state social assistance into a unified system and raised its spending nearly ten-fold.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Vision rejects 'any sort of prejudice against any nation' and pledges to treat the peoples of the region 'as our equals'.

class-collaboration.rationale: The programme's 'biggest target' in labour is social dialogue and solving problems 'through mutual agreements' among workers, employers and government for labour peace.

clerical-rule.rationale: The programme defines Turkey as a secular, democratic state in which sovereignty belongs to the people and rejects using religion for political ends.

close-ties-china.rationale: The programme wants relations with powers built 'flexibly and with many axes' and closer ties with China and East Asia.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The programme says Turkey 'is respectful of the territorial integrity and sovereignty of other countries'.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Vision reports that collective bargaining for public servants 'has already been realized' and promises a law protecting collective bargaining.

collective-defense.rationale: The programme pledges to maintain Turkey's contributions inside NATO and its defence cooperation with allies.

collective-farming.rationale: The programme wants agricultural units turned into economic enterprises, backed by insurance, commodity exchanges and private forestry, not collective farms.

communal-electorates.rationale: The Vision rejects 'divisive identity politics' built around one religion or sect.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The programme strengthens local government within 'the unitary State structure'.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Vision says 'conservative democracy values political legitimacy based on the will of the people' and that no one may exercise sovereign power without basing it on that will.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The programme laments a Turkey 'where materialistic concerns are at the forefront' and spiritual elements are pushed aside.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The programme rests on a market economy, private enterprise and guaranteed property rights.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The programme seeks to solve labour problems 'through mutual agreements, within a triple structure consisting of the worker, employer and the government', though it says nothing of setting prices.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The Vision reports new policies 'to heal the wounds of all discriminatory practices previously meted out to religious, ethnic and social groups' and the end of assimilation policies.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The programme says winning power 'does not make the will of the majority absolute', but the Vision attacks judicial readings of the constitution as tutelage over the people's will.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments raised social spending sixteen-fold since 2002 and social assistance nearly ten-fold, and pledges to keep strictly to the principles of a social state.

decide-locally.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments quintupled municipal resources and pledges to keep delegating power from the centre to local agencies, within a unitary state.

delink-world-market.rationale: The programme wants foreign capital, exports and international competitiveness to drive development.

democracy-best.rationale: The Vision presents conservative democracy as resting on the will of the people expressed in free elections, and Çağlıyan-İçener cites Erdoğan calling democracy 'the perfect arrangement invented by humankind'.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The programme says democracy is more than voting, and Aslan shows the party rejecting a 'mechanical democracy' reduced to elections for an 'advanced' one.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: The programme calls competition of preferences crucial to democracy, but the Vision wants politics based on 'compromise ... rather than conflict and polarization'.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Vision names totalitarian and authoritarian approaches 'enemies of democratic politics' and requires power to rest on the will of the people.

direct-action.rationale: The Vision locates the people's will in 'free and fair elections' and parliament and describes change through elections, referenda and legislation.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The Vision reports that under AKP rule 'electing the president by public vote was approved', replacing election by parliament.

direct-votes.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments gave referenda 'due importance' so that participation is not limited to elections, while government stays representative.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The programme pledges to eliminate 'discriminatory provisions against women in our regulations' and to encourage women into public life and politics.

distribute-by-need.rationale: The Vision says 'we will all earn our bread with our own efforts, make it bigger and distribute it fairly', within a market economy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The programme says cultural activities in languages other than Turkish reinforce 'the unity and integrity of our country, rather than weaken it', calling diversity a richness.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The programme says that in a democracy 'sovereignty belongs to the people', and the Vision calls the people's will 'the ultimate source of legitimacy'.

dominated-front.rationale: The Vision keeps EU full membership as a strategic goal and treats the US and NATO as partners, not as powers to front against.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme welcomes foreign capital, an export drive and integration with world markets.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The programme treats citizens of every religion, sect and ethnic origin as first-class citizens.

elective-rulers.rationale: The programme says final authority rests with organs created through elections and that in a democracy 'sovereignty belongs to the people'.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments abolished emergency rule (OHAL) and State Security Courts and says they 'never sacrificed freedom for the sake of security'.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The programme pledges to maintain Turkey's NATO contributions and US defence cooperation, and the Vision treats the US and NATO as equal partners.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The programme says the majority 'will in no circumstances make the fundamental rights and freedoms a topic of discussion', and the Vision wants rights placed beyond the constitution and the state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The programme says that in democracies no citizens may enjoy higher rights or privileges and that citizens 'live freely under the equal protection of the laws'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The Vision calls ethnic, religious and regional nationalisms 'red lines' it rejects, and Aslan quotes Erdoğan: 'We oppose ethnic nationalism and refute racism', with citizenship as the overarching identity.

every-country-ready-for-democracy.rationale: The Vision says the Arab revolutions overcame 'centuries-old prejudices against the Middle Eastern people' by basing politics on the people's will.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme says 'oil and natural gas exploration shall be encouraged' and supports thermal power plants based on domestic coal.

expand-nuclear.rationale: The energy section states that 'nuclear energy power plants shall be built' with safety measures to supply inexpensive energy.

experts-over-public.rationale: The programme says 'no practice to shadow the will of the nation can be tolerated', and the Vision attacks the view that branded the people's will as 'politicization' to favour a bureaucratic oligarchy.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The programme calls deaths in custody and murders with unknown perpetrators unacceptable in a state of law and demands prosecution.

filial-duty.rationale: The programme pledges to 'encourage young generations to house their elderly parents' and incentives for family care of the elderly.

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: The Vision builds ties from the Balkans to Central Asia by making 'use of our historical heritage' and calls Turkey a centre that is 'making peace with its own history and geography'.

free-basic-services-for-all.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments made healthcare a state service to all 'regardless of income' with unconditional cover for children, while students got means-based aid or loans.

free-public-college.rationale: The programme plans a loan system so students at state universities 'can pay for their tuition and fees'.

free-trade.rationale: The Vision says 'we, as AK Party, have always defended market economy and free trade' and promises to keep supporting free trade.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The Vision plans a 'Commission for Equality and Fighting against Discrimination' and rejects 'all kinds of discrimination'.

future-generations.rationale: The programme makes public bodies responsible for 'preserving the natural resources and the environment from which future generations shall benefit'.

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: The Vision reports that the AKP government launched the Alliance of Civilizations with Spain in 2004 as a platform for coexistence of cultures.

gradual-change.rationale: The Vision describes the party's 'silent revolutions' as resting on 'an understanding of gradual change and societal dynamics'.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The programme wants 'an earnings system based on production rather than collecting interest', and the Vision says 'we will all earn our bread with our own efforts'.

indirect-election.rationale: Under AKP rule the election of the president was moved from parliament to a public vote, which the Vision reports as a democratic reform.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Vision speaks of 'religious, ethnic, social and cultural rights' exercised by groups and of healing discrimination against those groups.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme wants Turkey to become 'a country which produces constantly and which grows by producing', while managing the environmental cost of industrialization.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Vision treats political parties as indispensable and wants civil society organized in parties, NGOs and associations.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Aslan shows the party articulating democracy on 'its local values', while the Vision affirms universal democratic standards for all peoples.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The programme is 'respectful of the territorial integrity and sovereignty of other countries'.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The Vision calls Islamophobia 'a form of racism', and Çağlıyan-İçener shows the party presenting Turkey's Islamic identity as an enrichment for the EU.

land-redistribution.rationale: The programme promises 'guaranteed property rights' and plans agricultural modernization through enterprises and markets, not land seizure.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The programme guarantees property rights and backs private farming and forestry, though forest land stays state property with usage rights for villagers.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The programme deems it unacceptable to use religion for political ends, and Kaddorah describes the party's acceptance of not relying on Islamic law in legislation and affairs of state.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The programme refuses 'segregations borne by the Cold War period, based on the old political ideology'; the Vision calls the party a meeting point of different traditions.

limit-growth.rationale: The programme aims at sustainable growth while keeping 'the environmental cost of this development at a minimum', not at limiting growth.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The programme favours a market economy, says the state should in principle stay out of economic activity and calls privatization a vehicle for a more rational economy, while the Vision rejects 'the savagery of capitalism'.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Vision's 'Martyrs and Veterans' section promises a life with dignity to the families of soldiers who died for the country.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments appointed a civilian to head the National Security Council, opened military council decisions to judicial review and lifted the EMASYA protocol.

minority-language-support.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments opened native-language public broadcasting, lifted bans on campaigning in native languages and let state schools teach children their native languages.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The programme wants the south-east's problems solved 'within the scope of the general democratization project, rather than special arrangements aimed at the region', within the unitary state.

minority-veto.rationale: The programme accepts that those who win the majority's votes come to power, while protecting minority rights.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The programme opens public health to volunteer agencies and the private sector, has the state buy private schooling for poor pupils and wants services delivered with NGOs and private firms.

more-religion-public.rationale: Çağlıyan-İçener records AKP moves read as giving religion more public room (restricting alcohol sales, a proposal to allow headscarves in universities), against a declared refusal to politicize religion.

multipolar-world.rationale: The Vision expects 'inevitable changes' in the global system and wants Turkey among the countries shaping it, with 'no one' imposing its agenda.

municipal-property.rationale: The programme backs private ownership and privatization within a market economy.

nation-first.rationale: The programme seeks 'a balance between these realities and its national interests', and the Vision pairs national interest with a 'win-win' foreign policy of partnership, a deliberate middle.

national-church-status.rationale: The Vision's secularism keeps the state at equal distance from all religions and prevents one group's dominance.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Vision reports making European Court of Human Rights decisions a criterion for appointing judges and bringing law into line with the European Convention.

national-mission.rationale: The Vision says Turkey 'is destined to play a historic and critical role' and will support the democratization of neighbouring countries; Çağlıyan-İçener notes the 'mission' of proving a Muslim society can modernize.

national-resource-control.rationale: The mining programme emphasizes 'our national interests' yet says 'foreign capital shall be encouraged'.

national-self-determination.rationale: The programme upholds the Turkish Cypriots' right to self-determination yet insists on the unitary state at home and treats regional demands within general democratization.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Vision says the party 'always defended market economy' while never giving in 'to the savagery of capitalism', a market position rather than a third system.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Vision wants a deterrent national defence and honours soldiers who died for the country.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The record goes far beyond defence and justice: the Vision reports universal health insurance, 12-year compulsory schooling and a sixteen-fold rise in social spending under AKP governments.

no-business-privileges.rationale: The programme fights favoritism, partisanship and unfair profiteering and wants 'equal advantages to anyone'.

no-central-bank.rationale: The programme coordinates economic policy with the Central Bank and expects it to keep monetary stability.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The programme refuses to use sacred religious values for political purposes, and Aslan quotes the party: founding a party 'in the name of religion' is 'a misdeed to society and religion'.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The programme promises that 'the habit of not obeying rules shall be eliminated' and that laws bind everyone.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: As 'a requirement of the principle of secularism', the programme provides for citizens to learn their religion, keeping Religious Culture lessons and adding optional religion lessons.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Vision proposes debating a 'party-affiliated presidency', a semi-presidential or a presidential system, all with a political head of state.

office-by-exam.rationale: The programme makes 'career and merit' the basis of public recruitment and limits political replacement of officials.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments eased the conditions for forming new parties and made party closures harder, calling parties 'indispensable actors in a democracy'.

organic-representation.rationale: The Vision calls political parties 'indispensable actors in a democracy' and wants them freer to form and organize.

paid-care-work.rationale: The programme promises work for housewives to be covered by social security and to preserve 'respectability of household labor'.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The programme wants a parliament 'effective, independent and productive in legislative' work and laws expressing the common will.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The programme says democracy is 'a regime of participation and cooperation' in which citizens make, implement and control public decisions.

party-controls-media.rationale: The programme calls 'free, independent, multi-voiced' media one of the most important assurances of democracy and wants monitoring agencies kept from becoming 'political pressure vehicles'.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The programme promises that members may freely express their opinions and that binding group decisions are taken only 'in exceptional cases'.

pay-for-effort.rationale: The programme sets public salaries 'according to the task performed and their merits' and promises rewards for successful staff.

person-over-state.rationale: The Vision rejects 'the notion of people as a property of the state' and says 'people should own the state'; the programme's motto is 'let the people live so that the State can live'.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: The Vision says 'the realm of politics is based on a culture of compromise', though government still rests on majorities.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The programme says politics 'has become polluted' and that corruption stems from 'the misuse of political power', and Aslan shows the party contrasting the people with an out-of-touch Kemalist elite.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Vision says politics should rest on 'compromise, defragmentation and tolerance rather than conflict and polarization'.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: AKP governments passed the EU acquis reforms and opened accession negotiations in 2005; the Vision calls full membership the strategic goal, accepting no other option.

population-transfer.rationale: The programme holds that there is 'no obligation for differences to be converted to one another' and treats every citizen, of any origin, as first class.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The programme pledges 'maximum effort' to protect national values and preserve the basic structure of the national culture, and the Vision promises to support all activities strengthening 'our cultural values'.

price-stability-first.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments brought inflation to single digits and removed six zeros from the lira, and keeps fighting inflation a priority.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments multiplied social assistance spending nearly ten-fold and cut extreme poverty, aiming that no family lives below the poverty line by 2023.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The programme keeps 'foreign security, justice' among the basic functions from which the state must not withdraw.

production-for-use.rationale: The programme backs a market economy driven by private entrepreneurs who invest where they can make 'economic calculations'.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: The Vision pledges to 'support both the democratization and development' of neighbouring countries, though as conservative rather than liberal democracy.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The programme wants a 'State of law' instead of a 'State of codes', with laws applied as written and binding for everyone.

property-franchise.rationale: The programme promises 'the free right to elect and be elected of the citizens' with all its elements.

property-fundamental.rationale: Among its economic policies the programme lists 'guaranteed property rights' as part of a judicial order conforming to universal standards.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Vision reports continued financial aid and water and power projects for the Turkish Cypriots.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Vision reports that AKP governments passed the law on the Right to Access Information for transparent government.

public-ownership.rationale: The programme says the state should remain outside all economic activities and pledges to privatize energy facilities 'in the soonest time' and harbour services.

racial-franchise.rationale: The programme's democracy rests on universal citizenship that embraces citizens of every ethnic origin equally.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Vision says identity politics centred on one religion, sect or ethnic identity 'polarized politics' and rejects it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The programme embraces all citizens 'as first class citizens, regardless of differences in religion, language, sect, regional origin, ethnic origin or sex' and lists racism among evils to fight.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The programme calls religion 'one of the most important institutions of humanity', and Kaddorah quotes Erdoğan seeking a rationalism 'that does not disregard the spiritual meaning of life'.

rehabilitation.rationale: The programme says penal institutions 'shall be modernized to regain the criminal for the society', while also asking for a deterrent posture towards criminals.

religion-illusion.rationale: The programme considers religion 'one of the most important institutions of humanity'.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Çağlıyan-İçener records the AKP's proposal to allow girls wearing headscarves into universities.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Vision says secularism keeps the state 'in equal distance to all religions and religious groups' and prevents 'the dominance of one religious group over others'.

religious-nation.rationale: The programme makes 'being a citizen of the Republic of Turkey' the cement of society, whatever a citizen's religion.

remove-other-ethnic-groups-from-country.rationale: The programme embraces citizens of every ethnic origin as first class and rejects racism.

replace-appointed-officials.rationale: The programme wants officials appointed on career and merit, with only legally defined top posts changing with governments.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Vision says its conservatism 'is not the protection of the status quo' but of perennial values, and Kaddorah notes it no longer means 'returning and clinging to the past'.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The Vision holds that a strong economic system is not possible 'without a strong democracy based on the rule of law', treating the two as one coin.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The Vision pledges to widen 'hate crimes' to all speech containing religious and ethnic hate, insult and provocation and to 'introduce strong measure to ban hate speech'.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The programme promises to extend the freedoms of collective bargaining and strikes to public employees.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The programme promises to work 'in the platform of the contemporary democratic values, rather than ideological platforms' and says AK Parti 'is not and shall not be a party forcing ideologies'.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The Vision reports Turkey's humanitarian aid reaching 'a vast geography', including a major aid campaign for Somalia.

right-to-secede.rationale: The programme defends 'the unity and the integrity' of the Republic and the unitary state, and Aslan quotes the party: 'one nation, one flag, one country, one state'.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Vision requires every person or institution exercising sovereign power to base it on the will of the people.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The programme pledges to protect the historical texture of cities and national culture, and the Vision promises to protect historical heritage and deepen activities promoting the cultural legacy.

school-vouchers.rationale: The programme says the state 'shall buy services' so poor families can send their children to private schools, success being the criterion.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The programme says torture, deaths in custody, disappearances and unsolved murders 'shall be seriously prosecuted' and 'those responsible shall not go without punishment'.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The record points both ways: the Vision reports paying off the IMF and weathering the crisis without bailouts, but also attracting more foreign capital than the economy needed.

separate-church-state.rationale: The programme makes secularism the state's impartiality towards all beliefs and a prerequisite of democracy, but rejects the strict, assertive laicism that bars religion from public life (Aslan).

separated-powers.rationale: The programme says 'the principle of the separation of the powers shall be implemented meticulously' with checks and balances, and the Vision wants absolute separation of legislature and executive.

shared-human-nature.rationale: The Vision grounds politics in 'the sanctity of the human person' and universal human rights.

single-official-language.rationale: Turkish stays the official language, but the Vision reports that AKP governments lifted bans on other languages in broadcasting, campaigning and schooling.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The Vision says change 'should be achieved by protecting the core values and gains of traditional structures', rejecting radicalism.

social-market-economy.rationale: AKP governments let the private sector lead growth while raising social spending sixteen-fold, as the Vision reports: market economy and free trade, but 'never... the savagery of capitalism'.

socialized-care.rationale: The programme expands rest homes and child-care centres but also encourages families to house and care for their elderly.

socialized-markets.rationale: The programme backs privatization and privately owned enterprise as the engine of production, the opposite of requiring worker or public ownership.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The programme says 'the principle that the Constitution and the laws are binding for everyone shall be meticulously applied'.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The programme wants to enrich 'our spiritual world' against materialism, and Erdoğan, quoted by Kaddorah, values 'the spiritual meaning of life'.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Vision reports AKP governments' 'successful fight against the mafia and other illegal organizations' and the struggle against PKK terrorism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme keeps the state out of economic activity, yet it also promises incentives for strategic sectors (defence, space, automotive) and makes the defence industry a priority.

state-harmful.rationale: The programme calls security 'the State's most essential and crucial function' and gives the state duties of justice, welfare and basic services.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The programme rejects 'the interpretation and distortion of secularism as enmity against religion' and provides religious instruction.

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: The Vision says the state should not 'impose its preferences onto its citizens', yet it promises to strengthen marriage and raise children 'pious' and moral.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The programme keeps Turkey in NATO and seeks its place in the European security and defence framework.

strong-leader.rationale: The Vision blames weak coalitions for crises and asks for a 'stable, effective and powerful executive' able to take fast decisions, but also wants it controlled by the legislature and calls authoritarian approaches enemies of democracy.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Kaddorah finds the AKP aiming at a secularism like the Swiss or American models, as an alternative to the laïcisme in which 'the state controls religion'.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The programme says 'securing the views of the minority and the right to oppose' strengthens democracy's pluralism.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: The record mixes means-tested aid (a points system and minimum income by poverty level) with universal provision such as general health insurance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The Vision commits to free trade and free capital movements and to raising international competitiveness rather than protection.

taxation-theft.rationale: The programme defines taxes as the public sharing 'with the State a portion of the value it produces' and asks for fairer, simpler taxes, not an end to them.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Vision wants a society 'that combines tradition and modernity, the local and the global', and Çağlıyan-İçener describes conservative democracy as a synthesis of tradition and modernity.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The Vision seeks wider regional influence and global activism, but the programme is 'respectful of the territorial integrity and sovereignty of other countries'.

total-state.rationale: The Vision says the state 'should not define, shape or impose its preferences onto its citizens' and should be small, while conservative democracy treats totalitarianism as an enemy.

traditional-family.rationale: The programme calls the family 'the foundation of society', the Vision says 'as a conservative democrat party, we value family', and Kaddorah reports that theorist Akdoğan sees it as society's most important institution.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The programme speaks of a people 'living within the same geography for millennia' with 'a deep rooted and rich tradition of government'.

unions-good.rationale: The programme promises that 'unionization shall be promoted' and that public employees will gain union rights, collective bargaining and the right to strike.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 2012 Political Vision reports that AKP governments introduced General Health Insurance in 2012, gave all under-18s unconditional cover and made decent healthcare 'a service to all citizens by the state, regardless of income'.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The programme accepts the secular democratic state and rejects using religion for political ends.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme aims to rebuild the middle class through tradesmen, artisans and small firms, protecting them from unfair competition by large corporations, and offers privatized shares first to employees and local people.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The programme encourages women and the young to take part actively in public life and politics.

women-must-cover.rationale: The programme deems it unacceptable 'to put pressure on people who think and live differently by using religion'.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The programme commits to implementing CEDAW and eliminating 'discriminatory provisions against women in our regulations'.

women-suffrage.rationale: The programme pledges to encourage women to take part in public life and 'play an active role in politics' and to remove discriminatory provisions.

worker-ownership.rationale: The programme names private entrepreneurs as 'the driving force of production' and backs privatization; worker shares appear only as first offers to employees of privatized firms.

workers-councils.rationale: The programme places final decision and executive authority in organs created through elections and wants an effective, independent parliament.

missingStatements.text: A state can be secular in its institutions without being hostile to religion or to religious believers.
missingStatements.rationale: The programme calls secularism a prerequisite of democracy while rejecting its reading as enmity against religion and opposing discrimination against the pious.
missingStatements.declined: Near-universal agreement (few ideologies would deny a state can be secular without hostility to religion), so it would not be contested; the audit's nuance is captured by separate-church-state.

The first pass (claude-sonnet-5-5, 2026-10-20) read part of the programme, the first part of the Wikipedia article and abstracts; under rules 5 Wikipedia is not evidence and inferences are not answers, so every first-pass answer was re-answered from the sources below or nulled, with the first version kept in each statement's reviewHistory (s2-s4 stay listed for that history). This pass read in full the AKP programme (s1), the 2012 Political Vision (s5/s6), Çağlıyan-İçener (s7), Kaddorah (s9) and Aslan (s10). The AKP site and the ACRPS site refuse scripted access, so the Vision and the ACRPS paper are cited from Wayback Machine copies. Record over words: the acts of AKP governments up to 2012 reported in the Vision and by Çağlıyan-İçener answer on their own (s6, s8); later practice and critics' accounts (media freedom, the 2013 protests, the presidential system) are not in these defining sources and are left out, so the profile describes the doctrine and its first decade. Akdoğan's book and the 2004 symposium proceedings were not available online. Themes searched: government and liberty (programme sections 2-4, Vision 'Politics, Democracy, Constitution and Rights'), economy (programme section 3, Vision 'Economy'), society and culture (programme section 5, Vision 'Society'), world (programme section 6, Vision 'The World'), religion and secularism (all sources), ecology and technology (programme sections 3.10, 5.11, 5.12). Nothing was found on sexuality, abortion, drugs, guns, immigration levels, criminal sentencing or most technology questions, which stay null.
